title: The library at a crossroads
description: One small budget. Two persuasive proposals. What would count as good evidence?

nodes.title: A decision for Monday
nodes.body: You are advising a fictional neighbourhood library. There is £3,000 for either evening opening hours or a weekend digital-skills club. The committee wants a recommendation. All figures in this story are invented for learning.

nodes.title: A very confident survey
nodes.body: Of 40 people surveyed inside the library on Tuesday morning, 32 prefer evening hours. A volunteer says: ‘That is 80% of the community.’ But people who cannot visit during the day were never asked.

nodes.title: The numbers tell a story — but which one?
nodes.body: Attendance rose during a month with a digital-skills event. That month also had school holidays and a new local bus route. The records show who attended, not why attendance changed.

nodes.title: Who is missing from the evidence?
nodes.body: Which interpretation of the Tuesday survey is most defensible?

quiz.explanation: A convenience sample of current daytime visitors may miss workers, non-users and people facing access barriers. A large percentage alone does not establish representativeness.

options.label: 80% proves the whole community prefers evenings
It describes respondents; broader outreach is needed

nodes.title: Did the event cause the increase?
nodes.body: Attendance increased in the month of the digital-skills event. What can you conclude from these records alone?

quiz.explanation: An association cannot isolate the event’s effect. Holidays and transport changes are plausible alternative explanations. A comparison and baseline would strengthen a future evaluation.

options.label: The event definitely caused the increase

nodes.title: Make a recommendation
nodes.body: There is time for a modest pilot before committing the full budget. Which proposal best supports learning while respecting residents?

quiz.explanation: A time-limited pilot with a baseline, outreach to non-users and anonymous feedback can inform a decision. It still cannot guarantee causality or represent every resident.

options.label: Spend everything immediately based on the 80%
Pilot both options, define measures and invite missing voices

nodes.title: A recommendation with room to learn
nodes.body: Your next step is a small, clearly documented pilot: compare participation with a baseline, record access barriers and invite voluntary anonymous feedback. Report uncertainty alongside results. Revisit your choices below: a responsible decision is one you can explain and revise.
